canvas-01.description: The map on the lower half of the first page of the Somers Point atlas covers the south side of Bay Avenue between New Jersey Avenue and New York Avenue, down to the shore of Great Egg Harbor Bay. The upper half of the page carries the title cartouche, the water and fire department report, the key, the street and specials index, a small key map of the whole town at about 1200 feet to an inch and a New Jersey locator map; that half is not part of this map and is masked off along the heavy dividing line. Bay Avenue runs along the top edge and only its south side is drawn. Higbee, Gibbs and Cleveland Avenues run from Bay Avenue toward the water, with New Jersey Avenue at the left edge and New York Avenue, marked not open, at the right edge. The blocks are numbered 168 to 171 and are thinly built with frame dwellings and garages. The Seaside Theatre, a concrete-block building with steam heat and electric lights, stands on Bay Avenue between Higbee and Gibbs Avenues, and a club house stands west of Higbee Avenue. The shore line crosses the lower left of the map diagonally, with a public pier on piles and a pavilion at the end of New Jersey Avenue. The scale is 50 feet to an inch; the margins along the water and the bottom are marked no exposure.
notes: Seaside Theatre on Bay Avenue between Higbee and Gibbs Avenues.
New York Avenue is marked not open.
Cleveland Avenue has no junction with Bay Avenue in the modern reference data.
Bay Avenue is the boundary street of the map; three of its four junctions were hand-picked as the drawn south edge plus half the 50 ft width.

Sheet 1, 50 ft. Upper half of the page is the title, water and fire report, key, street and specials index, a 1200 ft key map of the town and a New Jersey locator (not configured: key map at 1200 ft). Lower half is a to-scale map: south side of Bay Av from New Jersey Av to New York Av (not open), Higbee, Gibbs and Cleveland Avs, down to the Great Egg Harbor Bay shore; Seaside Theatre. Bay Av is the boundary street (north side not drawn). One part, masked below the heavy dividing line.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the southwest end of Somers Point where the road from the Great Egg Harbor Bay bridge enters the town. Shore Road (Main Avenue) comes in over an iron bridge across the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad, electric and steam), which curves across the middle of the sheet to a transformer station and depot. Main Avenue runs south from the bridge to the water, and Broadway, Decatur Avenue (not open) and Braddock Avenue lead off to the northwest. East of the railroad George Avenue, Annie Avenue and Somers Avenue run from Shore Road to Bay Avenue, with Arnold Road (arbitrary) north of Shore Road. The sheet is a resort and hotel district: the large Gateway Casino with its kitchen stands by the water on Main Avenue, with The Bay Shores, Somers Point Inn, Schick's Hotel and Roberts Hotel nearby, and Somers Mansion stands north of Shore Road. Lake and Risley Co. lumber sheds and the Anglers Club lie north of Shore Road near Arnold Road. South of Bay Avenue the shore of Great Egg Harbor Bay is drawn with wooden bridges and piers on piling. The rest is dwellings on large lots. Scale 50 feet to an inch.
notes: George Avenue is now George Street.
Gateway Casino, Somers Point Inn, Schick's Hotel, Roberts Hotel, The Bay Shores and Somers Mansion are on this sheet.
Iron bridges carry Shore Road over the railroad; the area west of George Avenue has since been rebuilt around the Somers Point circle and MacArthur Boulevard.
Decatur Avenue is marked not open; Arnold Road is marked arbitrary.

Sheet 2, 50 ft. Southwest end of town at the bridge: Shore Rd (Main Av) from the Iron Bridge, Main Av, Broadway, Decatur Av (not open), Braddock Av, Arnold Rd (arbitrary), George Av (now George Street), Annie Av, Somers Av, Bay Av; W.J.&S.R.R. (P.R.R.) crossing; Gateway Casino, Somers Point Inn, Schick's Hotel, Roberts Hotel, Somers Mansion, Bay Shores, Lake & Risley Co., Anglers Club. The area west of George Av has been rebuilt around the Somers Point circle and MacArthur Boulevard; no junction used there.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the centre of Somers Point between Shore Road (Main Avenue) at the top and Bay Avenue and the shore of Great Egg Harbor Bay at the bottom, from Arnold Road (arbitrary) and Somers Avenue on the left to New Jersey Avenue on the right. Elk Place and Echo Place, both marked arbitrary, run between the blocks. Shore Road is the commercial street: the City Hall with Fire Department Station No. 2, the Post Office, Hotel Davis, a printing shop, an auto repairing garage and stores line it, and The Waverly stands on the north side near Arnold Road. The blocks between Shore Road and Bay Avenue are filled with frame dwellings. On Bay Avenue are the Anchorage Hotel and a large concrete garage for forty cars; across Bay Avenue, on the water, stands the Grand View Hotel of Milton Latz, marked vacant, beside a row of small buildings on a pier. Piers on piles run out into the bay. The north edge of the sheet shows the long lots of block 41A running back from Shore Road. Scale 50 feet to an inch.
notes: City Hall and Fire Department Station No. 2 on Shore Road near New Jersey Avenue.
Anchorage Hotel on Bay Avenue; Grand View Hotel (Milton Latz) marked vacant.
Elk Place, Echo Place and Arnold Road are marked arbitrary and are not in the modern reference data.

Sheet 3, 50 ft. Shore Rd (Main Av) and Bay Av between Arnold Rd (arbitrary) and New Jersey Av: Somers Av, Elk Pl and Echo Pl (arbitrary, not in the reference data), Delaware Av; City Hall and Fire Dept. Station No. 2, Post Office, Hotel Davis, The Waverly, Anchorage Hotel, Grand View Hotel (Milton Latz, vacant); bay shore and piers.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the blocks between Shore Road (Main Avenue) and Bay Avenue from New Jersey Avenue east to New York Avenue, a residential district south of the town centre. Higbee Avenue and Gibbs Avenue run straight from Shore Road to Bay Avenue, Cleveland Avenue starts south of Sunny Avenue, and Sunny Avenue cuts in at the right toward New York Avenue. Pennsylvania Avenue meets Shore Road from the north. The blocks, numbered 147 to 149, are divided into narrow lots and built up with frame dwellings and garages. Stores, an auto repair shop of concrete block and a few two-storey buildings stand on Shore Road between New Jersey and Higbee Avenues; the rest is houses. Water pipes are drawn in Shore Road and the cross avenues. Along the bottom edge the north fronts of the blocks south of Bay Avenue are outlined without detail, and the right margin shows the edge of the neighbouring sheet. Scale 50 feet to an inch.
notes: New Jersey and New York Avenues are now East New Jersey and East New York Avenues south of Shore Road; Pennsylvania Avenue is West Pennsylvania Avenue.
Shore Road meets West and East New York Avenue at two junctions about 12 m apart; both were detected.
Sheet 4, 50 ft. Shore Rd (Main Av) to Bay Av between New Jersey Av and New York Av: Higbee, Gibbs, Cleveland Avs, Sunny Av at the right; Pennsylvania Av meets Shore Rd from the north.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the blocks north of Shore Road (Main Avenue) between New Jersey Avenue and New York Avenue. Third, Second and First Streets cross the upper part of the sheet, with Pennsylvania Avenue running through the middle; the blocks are numbered 84 to 97 and are thinly built with frame dwellings and garages on deep lots, several blocks still empty. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad, electric and steam) crosses the sheet below First Street. Between the railroad and Shore Road lie blocks 100 and 101 with the First Baptist Church, stores and dwellings facing Shore Road and a passenger station by the tracks near New York Avenue; Pennsylvania Avenue is marked not open there, and Center Street runs along part of block 101. The lower left corner shows part of block 41A and a brick building behind Shore Road. The strip between the railroad and Shore Road is drawn turned slightly against the blocks above it. Scale 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Center Street is now Centre Street.
New Jersey, Pennsylvania and New York Avenues north of Shore Road are now West New Jersey, West Pennsylvania and West New York Avenues.
First Baptist Church on Shore Road; passenger station of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad near New York Avenue.
Pennsylvania Avenue between the railroad and Shore Road is marked not open.

Sheet 5, 50 ft. North of Shore Rd between New Jersey Av and New York Av: 3rd, 2nd and 1st Sts, Pennsylvania Av (not open south of the railroad), Center (now Centre Street); W.J.&S.R.R. (P.R.R.) across the sheet; First Baptist Church, passenger station. The strip between the railroad and Shore Rd is drawn about 2.5 degrees turned against the upper blocks; it fitted within 1 to 2 m as one part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the northwest residential grid of Somers Point at 100 feet to an inch, from First Street at the bottom to Seventh Street at the top and from Pennsylvania Avenue on the left to Massachusetts Avenue and Marks Road on the right. New York Avenue, Fox Terrace, Connecticut Avenue and Rhode Island Avenue run across the numbered streets, and Marion Place and Tudor Terrace are short streets in the upper right. The blocks, numbered 61 to 99, are laid out in lots and only partly built, with scattered frame dwellings and garages; several blocks are empty. The public school stands at New York Avenue and First Street, and the Water Works pumping station with its stand pipe is on Fifth Street at Connecticut Avenue. Marks Road crosses the lower right corner diagonally, and the large block 94 east of Rhode Island Avenue is open land. Bethel Road and the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad, electric and steam) run along the bottom edge.
notes: Public school at New York Avenue and First Street; Water Works pumping station at Fifth Street and Connecticut Avenue.
Pennsylvania, New York and Connecticut Avenues are now West Pennsylvania, West New York and West Connecticut Avenues.
Fifth Street / Tudor Terrace was rejected at 8 m; Marion Place is not in the modern reference data.

Sheet 6, 100 ft. Grid from 1st St to 7th St between Pennsylvania Av and Massachusetts Av: New York Av, Fox Terrace, Connecticut Av, Rhode Island Av, Marion Pl, Tudor Ter, Marks Rd, Bethel Rd at the bottom corner; Public School, Water Works pumping station.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the area from the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad and First Street south across Shore Road (Main Avenue) to the harbor, between New York Avenue and Maryland Avenue (Shady), at 100 feet to an inch. North of Shore Road, Center Street and Bethel Road frame blocks 102 to 104 with the Raymond Smith millwork plant, the Peter Somers cinder block works, Fire Department Station No. 1 and a national bank. South of Shore Road stand the Atlantic Shores Sanitarium Hospital, the Methodist Protestant Church and a Roman Catholic church along Connecticut Avenue and Harbor Lane, which runs diagonally south to Bay Avenue and Yacht Avenue. Sunny, Sunset and Sunrise Avenues and Pleasant Avenue lay out mostly empty blocks in the east. South of Bay Avenue the land is marsh, with Brighton Avenue and Atlantic Avenue marked not open, a creek with boat basins, and a tourist camp and auto repair building on Bay Avenue near Maryland Avenue. Along the harbor shore Launch Avenue, Miller Avenue and Kapella Avenue serve a small settlement with a boat storage yard and wooden piers.
notes: Atlantic Shores Sanitarium Hospital on Shore Road at New York Avenue; the site is now the Shore Medical Center.
Harbor Lane south of Shore Road is now East Harbor Lane and appears realigned: its junctions were 4 to 14 m off and were left out.
Kapella Avenue is spelled Kappella Avenue in the modern data; Maryland Avenue is East Maryland Avenue.
Atlantic Avenue and Brighton Avenue south of Bay Avenue are marked not open; Sunny and Sunrise Avenues east of Pleasant Avenue likewise.
Fire Department Station No. 1 on New York Avenue north of Shore Road.

Sheet 7, 100 ft. Shore Rd and south to the harbor between New York Av and Maryland Av (Shady): Center, Connecticut Av, Bethel Rd, Harbor La, Brighton Av, Sunny, Sunset, Sunrise, Bay, Atlantic (not open), Yacht, Miller, Kapella and Launch Avs, Pleasant Av; Atlantic Shores Sanitarium Hospital, Methodist Protestant Church, R.C. Church, Fire Dept. Station No. 1, Raymond Smith Millwork, Peter Somers cinder block works; marsh in the south. Harbor La has been realigned (residuals 4 to 14 m) and was left out.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the northeast part of Somers Point at 100 feet to an inch, between Maryland Avenue (Shady) and Dawes Avenue. Shore Road (Main Avenue) crosses the middle of the sheet, with Sunny Avenue and Bay Avenue below it and First Street (Atlantic Avenue) on both sides of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad above it; Launch Haven station is on the railroad. Groveland, Cedar, Johnson and Pierson Avenues run across, and in the upper left Bethel Road, Marks Road and Maple Avenue (not open) meet near a cement block works. The blocks, numbered 104 to 229, are built up with frame dwellings on narrow lots south of the railroad and more thinly to the north. The Raymond Smith lumber yard with its lumber piles lies beside the railroad, the Bell Telephone Exchange is on Johnson Avenue north of Shore Road, and the Dawes Avenue Public School stands on a large lot east of Pierson Avenue. Below Bay Avenue the bottom edge shows block outlines over marsh land. Several blocks are subdivided without buildings.
notes: Dawes Avenue Public School; Bell Telephone Exchange on Johnson Avenue; Raymond Smith lumber yard by the railroad.

First Street (Atlantic Avenue) lines both sides of the railroad; the modern data calls the north street 1st Street near Maryland and Groveland Avenues and both sides Atlantic Avenue further east, so the doubled Atlantic Avenue junctions at Johnson, Pierson and Dawes were excluded.
Dawes Avenue junctions at Sunny Avenue and Bay Avenue disagree with the fit by about 9 m or were not found; East Dawes Avenue may have been realigned.
The avenues are now East and West Maryland, Groveland, Cedar, Johnson, Pierson and Dawes Avenues on either side of Shore Road.
Maple Avenue is marked not open.

Sheet 8, 100 ft. Northeast part: Shore Rd, Sunny Av and Bay Av between Maryland Av (Shady) and Dawes Av, with Groveland, Cedar, Johnson, Pierson Avs; 1st St (Atlantic Av) on both sides of the W.J.&S.R.R.; Bethel Rd, Marks Rd and Maple Av at the top left; Dawes Av Public School, Bell Telephone Exchange, Raymond Smith Lumber Yard, cement block works.
